newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand likely to allow short selling in Q3.
newsitem.headline: Thailand likely to allow short selling in Q3.

text.p: Thailand's Securities and Exchange Commission said on Tuesday that stock market investors may be allowed to undertake short selling in about 25 listed companies by the third quarter of this year at the earliest.

"There will be about 25 shares in which short selling will be allowed initially. The Stock Exchange of Thailand will specify those shares," said Tipsuda Thavaramara, assistant director at the SEC's market supervision office.
She told a news conference that short selling would give an opportunity for investors to make profits on stock investments when markets were falling.
"The short selling will also add more liquidity and help the market," she said.
Profits generated by short selling by individual investors will be exempted from the country's capital gains tax, she said.
